extracted.intended_audience: Marine Corps and DoD contracting officers, A-76 program managers, installation commanders, and acquisition personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for conducting OMB Circular A-76 competitive sourcing (commercial activity) studies, including staffing, risk management, Performance Work Statements, cost comparisons, and program management for Marine Corps/DoD installations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing of Source Selection Team (SSEB/SSAC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The staffing of the Source Selection Evaluation Board (SSEB) and the Source Selection Advisory Council (SSAC) are critical decisions to which the contracting officer should have input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting officer role: ensure assignments do not impose conflicts of interest for Government employees or violate legal requirements. Comptroller General precedent demonstrates that failing to identify conflicts can jeopardize integrity and force restart of acquisition; avoid evaluators who could access/aid contractor proposals. Involve counsel familiar with contracting statutes to 'scrub' proposed team members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compile conflict-of-interest database / identify undesirable personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands should compile a conflict of interest database containing names of employees forbidden from working on A-76 studies and develop lists of 'undesirable' people with potential conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make this one of the first steps when establishing the A-76 study team. Command/program manager should compile desired personnel lists and undesirable lists; secure military lawyers to review lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk identification and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and manage risks inherent in competitive sourcing; study respondents often provided little data on risk identification and management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk identification is under-documented; contracting officers should systematically identify risks (employee reactions, PWS issues, solicitation communications, cost comparison errors, unauthorized changes) and implement mitigation steps (work breakdown structure-like systems, validation methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Performance Work Statement is a primary risk area and will dictate the success of A-76 studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PWS must comprehensively capture the work currently performed by Government employees. Failure to do so can negate anticipated savings and require contract amendments. Expected approach: use structured breakdown (work breakdown structure), validation methods, and solicit feedback (see draft solicitation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'gold plating' requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Gold plating' the requirements (over-specifying or adding unnecessary requirements) is a significant risk to competitive sourcing and can invite protests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not add excessive/unnecessary requirements beyond the true need; over-specification opens the command to protests by contractor and MEO. Review and validate PWS to avoid this anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for contract bundling/omnibus contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Bundling related activities into a single contract (omnibus contracts) can maximize economies of scale but risks excluding small or disadvantaged firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance economies of scale with statutory/small-business participation obligations. If bundling, consider subcontracting strategies or primary/diversified subcontractor structures to allow small/disadvantaged firms to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with small business policy (FAR 19.201)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is Government policy to provide maximum practicable opportunities in acquisitions to small business, HUBZone, small disadvantaged, and women-owned small business concerns, including subcontracting opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure acquisitions and solicitation strategies are consistent with FAR 19.201 to avoid excluding mandated sources; consider subcontracting and review bundling decisions with small-business impact in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Javits-Wagner-O’Day (JWOD) and FAR 8.704 precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: JWOD requires purchase of services from nonprofit organizations in the JWOD program; FAR 8.704 sets precedence for acquiring services first from JWOD firms, then Federal Prison Industries, Inc. (FPI), then commercial sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before issuing solicitations to commercial sources, confirm whether statutory preferential procurement programs require sourcing from JWOD/FPI; use draft solicitation steps to assess willingness to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use draft solicitation for industry comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuing a draft solicitation for industry comment can reveal whether mandatory sources will participate and yield valuable feedback on the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft solicitation allows assessment of JWOD/FPI/commercial participation, provides PWS feedback, and helps identify subcontracting opportunities to satisfy small-business requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage solicitation-phase communications (offerors and MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improper communications with offerors, the contractor, and the Most Efficient Organization (MEO) during solicitation phase are a critical risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure communications avoid 'technical leveling' and are tailored appropriately to the MEO. Maintain parity and documented, controlled communications to prevent protests and unfair advantage. Source selection procedures must mirror the standards stated in the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure source selection mirrors solicitation evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation criteria stated in the solicitation must be utilized in the source selection process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviations from solicitation criteria will result in protests and potential overturning of awards. Use documented evaluation procedures that align exactly with the solicitation and source selection plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict adherence to OMB A-76 cost comparison procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest award-phase risk is improper cost comparison between MEO and contractor proposals; contracting officers should strictly adhere to OMB A-76 steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to conduct correct cost comparisons can lead to reversals and appeals (example: Aberdeen Proving Grounds). Follow OMB A-76 cost-comparison principles precisely and document assumptions and methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent unauthorized changes to contracts post-award
rubrics_metrics.description: Increased interaction between Marines and contract employees raises the risk of unauthorized direction to contract employees to perform out-of-scope work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly instruct COTRs, commands, and Marines that only the contracting officer may change contract scope. Strengthen training/communication and oversight to prevent unauthorized work and manage post-award scope changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage risk of protests by following solicitation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Protests are a common risk and are managed by following solicitation procedures and using stated evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain strict compliance with solicitation terms, evaluation plans, and OMB A-76; document actions and rationales to defend awards. Deviations invite protests and potential reversal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify A-76 to allow capture/use of cost and past performance data (recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-76 should be modified to define practices for capturing cost and past performance data on Government organizations and allow incorporation of past performance into award decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes should permit contracting officers latitude to evaluate competitor past performance, technical approaches, management plans, and allow awards based on overall best value (not strictly lowest price). Implementation would align competitive sourcing closer to private-sector best-value decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish centralized database of best practices and lessons learned
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD should establish and maintain an Internet-accessible database of lessons learned and best practices from completed A-76 studies, resident within the Acquisition Web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services should be required to submit inputs at study closeout; primary focus should include study management, contracting issues, and PWS best practices to aid future studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish waiver procedures for mission-critical activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish waiver procedures to OMB A-76 that installation commanders can use to protect commercial activities they deem mission critical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver procedures would allow installation commanders to tailor competitive sourcing to local conditions and protect mission-critical functions while complying with higher-level listing/consolidation requirements (e.g., FAIR Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a program management approach for A-76 studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Marine Corps should adopt a program management approach (designate a program manager/ quasi program office) for conducting A-76 studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program manager responsibilities: unity of command, establish study timelines, program metrics, track progress (e.g., modified Earned Value Management), identify and mitigate risks, and retain sole authority to approve schedule deviations. Use integrated product teams (IPTs) plus a designated A-76 program manager for accountability and schedule control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components of Management Plan / Most Efficient Organization (MEO) development
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 studies require: development of a Performance Work Statement; conduct of a Management study to develop the Government's MEO; development of the in-house Government cost estimate; and conduct of a Cost Comparison between the MEO and lowest-priced responsible and responsive bidder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MEO is based on the Management Plan and PWS and is the basis for all Government costs entered on the Cost Comparison Form. The Management Plan outlines staffing patterns and operating procedures used for in-house cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measures and performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance measures are indicators (qualitative, quantitative, or other) that indicate whether current performance is reasonable and cost-effective; a Performance Standard reflects the minimum Federal requirement for performance of a commercial activity and incorporates quality and cost measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures can include workload/output-to-cost ratios, error rates, timeliness, user satisfaction, etc. Cost measures must reflect cost-comparability procedures to assure equity when comparing Government and private sector performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) definition/contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A PWS is a statement of the technical, functional and performance characteristics of the work to be performed; it identifies essential functions, performance factors, work units, quantities, and quality/timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PWS serves as the scope of work and is the basis for all costs entered on the Cost Comparison Form. Ensure clarity and completeness so MEO and contractors bid against the same requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-MEO Performance Review timing and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: When services are performed in-house as a result of a cost comparison, a formal Post-MEO Performance Review should be conducted, typically following the end of the first full year of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews confirm MEO implementation per the Transition Plan, establish MEO's ability to perform the PWS, and confirm that actual costs align with in-house cost estimates; adjustments may be made for mission or scope changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start date definitions for A-76 studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Start date may mean (1) date a cost comparison begins (typically when a local Study Team is formed and work on PWS/Management Plan/in-house estimate begins) or (2) the scheduled date work is to begin under a contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about which meaning is used in study documentation to avoid schedule/cost disagreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance Surveillance
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Assurance Surveillance is the method by which Federal employees supervise in-house or contract performance to ensure standards are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveillance should ensure standards are met as to quality and cost; distinguish surveillance from contract quality control, performance evaluation, or inspection (those can be commercial activities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferential procurement programs recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize special 'commercial' source programs (Preferential Procurement Programs) such as Federal Prison Industries and JWOD (Committee for the Purchase from the Blind and Other Severely Handicapped).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These programs have precedence in sourcing decisions; contracting officers must follow statutory ordering of preferred sources before procuring from other commercial sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples (catalog) of commercial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-exhaustive list of activities commonly treated as commercial: audiovisual services, ADP services, food services, health services, industrial shops, maintenance/repair/testing, management support, manufacturing, office/admin services, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the list (Appendix B) as guidance when determining whether an activity is commercial and subject to A-76 procedures, but analyze specific circumstances and statutory exceptions (inherently governmental functions, core capabilities).
